name: Mountains of Ararat
summary: Where the ark came to rest after the Flood.
note: Genesis names the mountains of Ararat (the ancient region of Urartu), not a single peak. The marker shows the modern Mount Ararat.

name: Babylon (Babel)
summary: Site of the tower of Babel in the land of Shinar; later Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar's capital, where Judah lived in exile.

name: Ur of the Chaldeans
summary: Abram's birthplace, a major Sumerian city near the Euphrates.

name: Haran
summary: Where Terah's family settled on the way to Canaan, and where Jacob later served Laban.

name: Shechem
summary: Abram's first stop in Canaan, where God promised him the land.

name: Bethel
summary: Where Abram built an altar and Jacob dreamed of a stairway to heaven.

name: Hebron (Mamre)
summary: Abraham's home by the oaks of Mamre, and the cave of Machpelah where the patriarchs were buried.

name: Sodom
summary: City of the plain where Lot lived, destroyed in judgment.
note: The location is disputed. The traditional view places it near the southern end of the Dead Sea; another proposal is Tall el-Hammam, northeast of the Dead Sea.

name: Gerar
summary: Philistine-region town where Abraham and later Isaac stayed.

name: Beersheba
summary: Well of the oath in the Negev, a home of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

name: Mount Moriah
summary: Where Abraham offered Isaac; later identified with the temple mount (2 Chronicles 3:1).
note: Genesis names "the land of Moriah"; 2 Chronicles 3:1 places Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah, and tradition joins the two. The exact hill of Genesis 22 isn't known.

name: Peniel (Penuel)
summary: By the Jabbok, where Jacob wrestled with God and was named Israel.

name: Dothan
summary: Where Joseph's brothers sold him to traders bound for Egypt.

name: Canaan
modernName: Israel, the West Bank and Lebanon's coast
summary: The land God promised to Abraham and his descendants, west of the Jordan River.

name: Sinai wilderness
summary: The desert peninsula between Egypt and Canaan where Israel traveled after the Exodus.

name: Egypt
summary: The great kingdom of the Nile, a place of refuge and later of slavery for Israel.

name: Goshen
summary: The fertile land in the eastern Delta where Jacob's family settled.

name: Rameses
summary: Store city built by Israelite labor, and the starting point of the Exodus.

name: Pithom
summary: Store city built by Israelite labor (Exodus 1:11).

name: Succoth
summary: Israel's first camp after leaving Rameses.

name: Etham
summary: Camp "on the edge of the wilderness" (Exodus 13:20).

name: Red Sea crossing (Yam Suph)
summary: Where God parted the sea and Israel crossed on dry ground.
note: Yam Suph means "Sea of Reeds." Proposed sites include the Bitter Lakes or Lake Timsah (shown), the Gulf of Suez, and the Gulf of Aqaba.

name: Marah
summary: Where God made bitter water sweet.

name: Elim
summary: Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

name: Wilderness of Sin
summary: Where God first gave manna and quail.

name: Rephidim
summary: Water from the rock and the battle with Amalek.

name: Mount Sinai (Horeb)
summary: The mountain of God, where Moses saw the burning bush and Israel received the covenant.
note: The traditional site is Jebel Musa in southern Sinai. Other proposals include Jebel al-Lawz in Arabia (ancient Midian) and Har Karkom in the Negev.

name: Midian
summary: Land east of the Gulf of Aqaba where Moses lived for forty years with Jethro.

name: Kadesh-barnea
summary: Oasis where Israel camped for many years and from where the spies were sent.

name: Mount Hor
summary: Where Aaron died, on the border of Edom.
note: Tradition places Aaron's tomb on Jebel Harun near Petra (shown). Many scholars look for Mount Hor nearer Kadesh, such as Har Zin, since Numbers 20 sets it on Edom's border a short march from Kadesh.

name: Plains of Moab
summary: Israel's final camp east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.

name: Mount Nebo
summary: Where Moses saw the Promised Land and died.

name: Jordan River
summary: The river Israel crossed into the Promised Land on dry ground, where John later baptized Jesus.

name: Gilgal
summary: Israel's first camp west of the Jordan, where they set up twelve stones from the riverbed.

name: Jericho
summary: The walled city whose walls fell after Israel marched around it for seven days.

name: Gibeon
summary: City that tricked Joshua into a treaty, where the sun stood still during the battle to defend it.

name: Shiloh
summary: Where the tabernacle stood through the time of the judges, and where Samuel grew up serving Eli.

name: Mount Tabor
summary: Rounded mountain above the Jezreel Valley where Barak gathered Israel's army.

name: Kishon River
summary: The stream that swept away Sisera's army (Judges 5:21), and where Elijah later killed the prophets of Baal.

name: Spring of Harod
summary: Where God cut Gideon's army down to three hundred men.

name: Bethlehem
summary: Town of Judah: home of Naomi and Boaz, birthplace of David, and birthplace of Jesus.

name: Moab
summary: Land east of the Dead Sea, home of Ruth and often an enemy of Israel.

name: Zorah
summary: Samson's hometown, in the hills facing Philistine country.

name: Gaza
summary: Philistine city where Samson brought down the temple of Dagon.

name: Ramah
summary: Samuel's home, where he was born and buried and where he judged Israel.
note: Samuel's Ramah (Ramathaim-zophim, 1 Samuel 1:1) is usually placed at al-Ram north of Jerusalem; some look for it further west.

name: Aphek
summary: Where the Philistines camped before capturing the ark of the covenant.

name: Jerusalem
summary: David's capital and the site of the temple: the center of Israel's worship, and where Jesus was crucified and rose again.

name: Gibeah
summary: Saul's hometown and capital, just north of Jerusalem.

name: Valley of Elah
summary: Valley in the Judean foothills where David fought Goliath.

name: Mount Gilboa
summary: Ridge above the Jezreel Valley where Saul and Jonathan died fighting the Philistines.

name: Dan
summary: Israel's northernmost city, where Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves.

name: Mount Carmel
summary: Ridge on the coast where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal.

name: Samaria
summary: Capital of the northern kingdom of Israel from Omri until its fall to Assyria.

name: Joppa
summary: Port where Jonah boarded a ship to flee from God, and where Peter raised Tabitha.

name: Nineveh
summary: Great capital of Assyria, which repented at Jonah's preaching and fell in 612 BC.

name: Tekoa
summary: Village in the Judean hills, home of the prophet Amos.

name: Lachish
summary: Judah's second city, besieged and taken by Sennacherib in 701 BC.

name: Anathoth
summary: Priestly town near Jerusalem, Jeremiah's home.

name: Chebar canal
summary: Canal in Babylonia where exiles from Judah lived and Ezekiel saw his visions of God's glory.

name: Susa
summary: Royal city of the Persian kings, where Esther became queen and Nehemiah served as cupbearer.

name: Tyre
summary: Phoenician island port, an ally of David and Solomon, later besieged by Nebuchadnezzar and taken by Alexander the Great.

name: Alexandria
summary: Alexander's city on the Nile Delta, home of a large Jewish community, where the Hebrew Scriptures were translated into Greek.

name: Nazareth
summary: Small Galilean village where Mary received the angel's message and Jesus grew up.

name: Sea of Galilee
summary: Freshwater lake where Jesus called fishermen as disciples, calmed the storm and walked on the water.

name: Capernaum
summary: Fishing town on the Sea of Galilee, Peter's home and the center of Jesus' Galilean ministry.

name: Bethsaida
summary: Fishing town at the north end of the Sea of Galilee, home of Peter, Andrew and Philip, near where Jesus fed the five thousand.
note: Usually placed at et-Tell; recent digs at el-Araj, nearer the shore, offer a rival site.

name: Bethany
summary: Village on the Mount of Olives, home of Mary, Martha and Lazarus.

name: Mount of Olives
summary: Ridge east of Jerusalem where Jesus taught, wept over the city, prayed in Gethsemane and ascended to heaven.

name: Gethsemane
summary: Olive garden at the foot of the Mount of Olives where Jesus prayed and was arrested.

name: Golgotha
summary: "The place of the skull" outside Jerusalem's wall, where Jesus was crucified and, nearby, buried.
note: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre has marked the site since the fourth century and is the likelier place. The Garden Tomb, north of the Damascus Gate, is a popular alternative.

name: Damascus
summary: Ancient Syrian city: Paul met the risen Jesus on the road there and was baptized there.

name: Caesarea
summary: Herod's port and the Roman capital of Judea, where Cornelius believed and Paul was held for two years.

name: Antioch (Syria)
summary: Great city of Syria, where believers were first called Christians and from where Paul set out on his journeys.

name: Antioch (Pisidia)
summary: Roman colony in Asia Minor where Paul first turned to the Gentiles.

name: Iconium
summary: City of Galatia where Paul and Barnabas preached until they were driven out.

name: Lystra
summary: Where Paul healed a lame man, was hailed as a god, then stoned; Timothy's hometown.

name: Derbe
summary: Easternmost city of Paul's first journey.

name: Philippi
summary: Roman colony in Macedonia, the first church in Europe, where Lydia believed and Paul and Silas sang in prison.

name: Thessalonica
summary: Capital of Macedonia, where Paul's preaching caused an uproar; he later wrote two letters to its church.

name: Athens
summary: Center of Greek learning, where Paul spoke to the philosophers at the Areopagus about the unknown god.

name: Corinth
summary: Wealthy port city of Greece where Paul stayed eighteen months; he wrote it at least two letters.

name: Ephesus
summary: Leading city of Asia, where Paul taught for over two years; the first of Revelation's seven churches.

name: Rome
summary: Capital of the empire, where Paul arrived as a prisoner and, by tradition, Peter and Paul were martyred.

name: Crete
summary: Large island south of the Aegean, where Paul left Titus to appoint elders in every town.

name: Malta
summary: Island where Paul's ship was wrecked on the way to Rome.

name: Patmos
summary: Small Aegean island where John, exiled for his witness, received the Revelation.

name: Smyrna
summary: Church of Revelation 2 facing persecution: "Be faithful unto death."

name: Pergamum
summary: Church of Revelation 2 living "where Satan's throne is."

name: Thyatira
summary: Church of Revelation 2, praised for its love and service; Lydia's hometown.

name: Sardis
summary: Church of Revelation 3 with a reputation for being alive, though it was dead.

name: Philadelphia
summary: Church of Revelation 3 given an open door that no one can shut.

name: Colossae
summary: Small Phrygian town in the Lycus valley, home of the church Paul wrote to and of Philemon.

name: Laodicea
summary: Wealthy church of Revelation 3, neither hot nor cold.

name: Seleucia
summary: Antioch's seaport, where Paul and Barnabas set sail on the first journey.

name: Salamis
summary: Port on the east coast of Cyprus, where Paul and Barnabas first preached in the synagogues.

name: Paphos
summary: Roman capital of Cyprus, where the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed.

name: Perga
summary: City of Pamphylia, where John Mark left Paul and Barnabas.

name: Attalia
summary: Port of Pamphylia, from which Paul and Barnabas sailed home to Antioch.

name: Troas
summary: Port near ancient Troy where Paul saw the vision of the man of Macedonia, and where Eutychus fell from a window.

name: Samothrace
summary: Mountainous island in the northern Aegean, Paul's first night's stop on the way to Europe.

name: Neapolis
summary: Port of Philippi, where Paul first set foot in Europe.

name: Amphipolis
summary: City on the Egnatian Way that Paul passed through on the way to Thessalonica.

name: Apollonia
summary: Town on the Egnatian Way between Amphipolis and Thessalonica.

name: Berea
summary: Town whose Jews "received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily."

name: Cenchreae
summary: Corinth's eastern port, home of Phoebe, where Paul cut his hair because of a vow.

name: Assos
summary: Port where Paul, having walked from Troas, rejoined the ship.

name: Mitylene
summary: Chief city of the island of Lesbos, a stop on Paul's last voyage to Jerusalem.

name: Miletus
summary: Port south of Ephesus where Paul said farewell to the Ephesian elders.

name: Cos
summary: Island off the coast of Caria, a night's stop on Paul's voyage to Jerusalem.

name: Rhodes
summary: Island port on the main sea lane between the Aegean and the east.

name: Patara
summary: Port of Lycia where Paul changed to a ship bound for Phoenicia.

name: Ptolemais
summary: Coastal city north of Mount Carmel where Paul spent a day with the believers.

name: Sidon
summary: Ancient Phoenician port, where the centurion let Paul visit his friends on the way to Rome.

name: Myra
summary: Port of Lycia where Paul was put on an Alexandrian grain ship bound for Italy.

name: Fair Havens
summary: Small harbor on Crete's south coast where Paul warned against sailing on.

name: Syracuse
summary: Great city of Sicily, where Paul's ship put in for three days.

name: Rhegium
summary: Port at the toe of Italy, on the strait facing Sicily.

name: Puteoli
summary: Italy's great port on the Bay of Naples, where Paul landed and found believers.

name: Gozan
summary: Town on the Habor River where Assyria resettled exiles from Israel.

name: Halah
summary: District in the Assyrian heartland where exiles from Israel were settled.

name: Riblah
summary: Nebuchadnezzar's headquarters in Syria, where Zedekiah was judged and blinded.

name: Judean wilderness
summary: Dry hills falling from Jerusalem to the Dead Sea, where David hid from Saul, John preached and Jesus was tempted.

name: Cana
summary: Galilean village where Jesus turned water into wine, his first sign.
note: Most scholars place Cana at Khirbet Qana; the town of Kafr Kanna, nearer Nazareth, is the traditional site.

name: Sychar
summary: Samaritan town near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman.

name: Caesarea Philippi
summary: Town at the springs of the Jordan below Mount Hermon, where Peter declared Jesus to be the Christ.

name: Emmaus
summary: Village about seven miles from Jerusalem, where the risen Jesus was known in the breaking of bread.
note: Several sites are proposed; Qalunya (Motza), about four miles from Jerusalem, and Emmaus Nicopolis, about twenty, are the leading candidates.
